label: הסבא מנובהרדוק – מהפכת המוסר של 'מדרגת האדם'

questions.question: True or false: Before he devoted himself to Torah, Rabbi Yosef Yozel Horowitz engaged in commerce in order to support his family.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: His father-in-law died between the betrothal and the marriage, and the burden of supporting the family, including his wife's sisters, was placed on him.

questions.question: Whom did he meet in the port city of Memel, in a meeting that changed his course?
options: Rabbi Israel Salanter, founder of the Mussar movement
The Alter of Kelm
The Chafetz Chaim
Rabbi Chaim of Brisk
questions.explanation: Rabbi Israel persuaded him to set most of his time for Torah study and invited him to a mussar lesson. He abandoned commerce and studied in the kollel in Kovno.

questions.question: For how long did he shut himself in a small house in Slobodka, without letting anyone enter?
options: One week
One year and nine months
Forty days
Seven years
questions.explanation: This was extreme withdrawal from the material world and its temptations.

questions.question: Who rebuked him that in times of spiritual crisis one must not seclude oneself alone?
options: Rabbi Israel Salanter
The author of "Arukh ha-Shulchan"
The Alter of Kelm, Rabbi Simcha Zissel Ziv
Rabbi Eliyahu Dov Berkovsky
questions.explanation: He accepted the rebuke, returned to the public and established study halls for Gemara and mussar in many communities.

questions.question: In which year did he found the Novardok yeshiva?
questions.explanation: In the Hebrew year 5656, in the city of Novardok in the Minsk province.

questions.question: True or false: The Novardok yeshiva opened with two hundred students.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: It opened with only ten. Within months there were about fifty, and two hundred only in 1899.

questions.question: True or false: The author of "Arukh ha-Shulchan," the rabbi of the city of Novardok, gave the yeshiva his backing against its opponents.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: Elements in the city demanded that the yeshiva be closed because of its moral approach, but Rabbi Epstein and the city's leaders stood by it.

questions.question: To where were two thirds of the yeshiva's young men transferred in 1908, and why?
options: To Zhetl, to keep them away from the dispute over the rabbinate in the city
To Gomel, because of the war
To Kiev, to help refugees
To Bialystok, for a new building
questions.explanation: After the death of Rabbi Epstein a dispute broke out over the rabbinic post. The young men returned when it subsided.

questions.question: How did the Alter of Novardok die?
options: He was killed in a pogrom
He contracted typhus while tending the sick in Kiev
He died in exile in Siberia
He died in old age in Jerusalem
questions.explanation: In 1919 he moved to Kiev to help the refugees, and he died on 17 Kislev 5680.

questions.question: True or false: The bones of the Alter of Novardok were brought up to Jerusalem and interred on Har HaMenuchot.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: His legacy continued also through his sons-in-law, among them Rabbi Avraham Yaffen, head of the Novardok yeshiva.

questions.question: True or false: According to the Alter of Novardok, one should rely on the natural intellect in working on the character traits.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: He held that the intellect distances a person from true self-work through excuses and vested interests, and therefore it must be subdued and the character traits worked on in practice.

questions.question: What was the purpose of the acts of "breaking the character traits" in Novardok?
options: To raise money for the yeshiva
To impress the residents of the city
To uproot the fear of the criticism of those around and to develop indifference to honor
To strengthen the body
questions.explanation: The best known of them are acts of public self-humiliation, intended to injure the inflated ego.

questions.question: What "bizarre" act did the Novardok students perform?
options: Fast for forty days
Deliver sermons in the town square
Disguise themselves as merchants
Enter a pharmacy and ask for nails
questions.explanation: They also deliberately dressed in worn clothing, in order to disconnect from the esteem of others.

questions.question: True or false: The Novardok students were careful to dress elegantly, in honor of the Torah.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: They deliberately wore worn and unelegant clothing, as part of the breaking of the character traits.

questions.question: What did Rabbi Yosef Yozel do when his candle went out as he was secluded in the forest?
options: He placed his trust in God, that if he deserved light it would be provided to him
He went out to the city to buy a candle
He stopped studying and went to sleep
He asked his students to bring a candle
questions.explanation: This is absolute trust, with the reduction of physical effort. According to the Novardok tradition his needs were indeed provided for.

questions.question: What is the name of his central book, the essence of his teaching?
options: "Mesillat Yesharim"
"Madregat ha-Adam"
"Duties of the Heart"
"Or Yisrael"
questions.explanation: After his death his discourses were studied in the Novardok yeshivas according to the months of the year, a different discourse each month.

questions.question: How were the discourses of "Madregat ha-Adam" written?
options: He wrote them himself in the years of his seclusion
They were written after his death from the students' memory
Students recorded his talks, and he chose the precise wording and corrected it
They were translated from Yiddish by his sons
questions.explanation: Usually he chose the notes of Rabbi Yitzchak Elchanan Waldshan. When he was not satisfied, he wrote the matter himself.

questions.question: What was the Chazon Ish's fundamental criticism of the institutional mussar path?
options: Mussar takes time away from prayer
Mussar is studied only in Kabbalistic books
Mussar is suitable only for householders
There is no inner change by a person's power alone; the inclination yields through subordination to halakha and theoretical study
questions.explanation: In his eyes the study of Torah itself breaks the character traits, without any need for external psychological systems.

questions.question: According to the research, what price did the extreme work on the character traits sometimes exact?
options: A feeling of worthlessness and harm to the joy of life among some of the students
A dispute with the authorities in Poland
Neglect of the study of Gemara
The departure of most of the students
questions.explanation: On the other hand, the iron resilience of those who endured it enabled the network to rehabilitate itself quickly after the First World War, in Poland and Latvia.

questions.question: What rupture did the Alter of Novardok identify and seek to heal?
options: A shortage of printed mussar books
A chasm that had opened between the sacred and the profane, and enthusiasm that had cooled even in the yeshivas
The multiplication of yeshivas in Lithuania
The dispute between Hasidim and Mitnagdim
questions.explanation: The solution: to restore to the yeshivas their power as in the days of Sura and Pumbedita, and "to establish whole Jews."
